title: National Aeronautics and Space Administration: Cybersecurity: NASA Needs to Fully Implement Risk Management
summary: GAO evaluated NASA cybersecurity risk management for selected projects and systems and issued sixteen recommendations. Entity test: The later records support a bounded remediation-workload and control-scope update but do not resolve control operation, incidents, recovery, or mission effects.
key_findings: GAO's public recommendation status said in May 2026 that NASA had not yet supplied sufficient evidence to close multiple control-assessment and risk-management recommendations.
Alternative-explanation test: Tests other remediation work, control scope, and tested-system differences.
Compatibility: Same agency and overlapping cybersecurity-control domain; recommendation inventories are not the annual FISMA maturity metric.
why_it_matters: This record either supplies a later compatible observation or tests a named Phase 56C alternative explanation without turning association into causal proof.
ftfn_relevance: Preserves the Phase 56C parent dossier and stable entity identifier.
Maps the record to named alternative explanations.
Separates observed result, attribution, independent validation, and unresolved denominators.
evidence_limits: The selected systems and recommendation statuses do not represent every NASA system, incident, recovery, service effect, or mission outcome.
Independent official oversight; closure is not inferred where evidence remained insufficient.
No causal effect, ranking, composite score, readiness score, or unsupported cross-entity comparison is supported.
